title: Lindbergh was not the first to fly nonstop across the Atlantic.
description:
Lindbergh was not the first to fly nonstop across the Atlantic. He flew solo from New York to Paris in over 33 hours and won the $25,000 Orteig Prize. Two men had crossed nonstop eight years earlier.

Alcock and Brown left Newfoundland in a converted bomber. They took off from Lester's Field near St John's at about 1:45 p.m. in a modified First World War Vickers Vimy.

About how long the crossing took, 1,890 miles from Newfoundland to Ireland.

They landed nose first in a bog. They aimed for what looked like a green field near Clifden, County Galway. It was Derrigimlagh Bog. The aircraft nosed over and neither man was hurt.

The Daily Mail paid 10,000 pounds. It was offered for a crossing in under 72 consecutive hours. A week later both men were knighted at Windsor Castle.

Alcock never saw 1920. He was killed on 18 December 1919 near Rouen, flying a new Vickers Viking amphibian to the Paris Airshow.

The first nonstop crossing came eight years before the famous one.

Established that the Vimy made 'the first non-stop flight across the Atlantic on 14th-15th June 1919', that the flight took 16 hours, that it ended in a crash-landing in a bog near Clifden, and that the crew were knighted by George V.
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Lindbergh: read. Established Lindbergh's solo flight of 20 to 21 May 1927 from Roosevelt Field to Le Bourget in over 33 hours, the $25,000 Orteig Prize, and that he was the first to fly nonstop from New York to Paris.
